questions.prompt: You calculate a commission in column C using a tax rate stored in cell F1, writing `=B2*$F$1`. After filling the formula down to row 10, what happens to the reference to F1?

options.text: It updates to $F$10 for each row.
It remains fixed at $F$1 for every row.
It becomes a relative reference to F2, F3, etc.
It causes a #REF! error.

questions.explanation: The dollar signs create an absolute reference, locking both the column and row so the rate cell stays constant when the formula is copied.

questions.prompt: A VLOOKUP formula returns a #N/A error even though you are confident the value exists in the table. What is the most likely cause regarding the lookup range settings?

options.text: The lookup range was defined without absolute references.
The range_lookup argument was omitted or set to approximate match instead of exact match.
The first column of the range does not contain the lookup value.
The data contains duplicate values in the first column.

questions.explanation: Without an explicit FALSE or 0 for exact match, VLOOKUP defaults to approximate match, which can fail if the data is not sorted or the range is wrong.

questions.prompt: You have a list of transactions with a 'Status' column containing 'Paid' or 'Pending'. You want a Pivot Table to count how many times each status appears. What should you drag into the Values area?

options.text: The Status column set to 'Summarize by Count'
The Amount column set to 'Summarize by Sum'
The Status column set to 'Summarize by Sum'
The Date column set to 'Count Unique'

questions.explanation: To count occurrences of text categories like statuses, you drag the field into Values and ensure it is summarized by Count, not Sum.

questions.prompt: Given the formula `=IF(A1>100, 'High', IF(A1>50, 'Medium', 'Low'))`, what result will be returned if cell A1 contains the value 75?

options.text: High
Medium
Low
Error

questions.explanation: 75 is not greater than 100, so it moves to the second condition; since 75 is greater than 50, it returns 'Medium'.

questions.prompt: You are dividing a total by a count that might be zero, risking a #DIV/0! error. Which function allows you to return a custom message instead of the error value?

options.text: IFERROR
ISERROR
ERROR.VALUE
IFNA

questions.explanation: IFERROR wraps the calculation and returns your specified value if any error occurs, including #DIV/0!, whereas IFNA only catches #N/A.

questions.prompt: You need to find a value in a table where the lookup key is located in a column to the right of the data you want to return. Why is INDEX/MATCH generally preferred over VLOOKUP here?

options.text: INDEX/MATCH can only search text values.
VLOOKUP can only look up values in the leftmost column of the range.
INDEX/MATCH is faster at summing large datasets.
VLOOKUP cannot handle numeric data.

questions.explanation: VLOOKUP requires the lookup column to be the first column in the range, while INDEX/MATCH allows flexible column ordering for both lookup and return.
